records.definition: Systems matching or exceeding human performance across most cognitive tasks, including ones outside their training distribution, without task-specific retraining.
AI systems that autonomously execute multi-step knowledge work across tools, queues and approval boundaries, owning outcomes end-to-end rather than assisting a human operator.
General-purpose physical robots (humanoid or otherwise) that are commercially routine, not demo-quality, with fleet-deployable reliability and workable unit economics.
Coding agents reliably owning the loop from ticket to monitored production deploy across large codebases, leaving humans mostly specifying, reviewing and steering.

records.reason: The threshold depends on the definition. We retain these windows as prompts for discussion. Neither a definition nor a benchmark result establishes a universal arrival year.

evidence.title: Google DeepMind: Levels of AGI
evidence.finding: This framework distinguishes breadth and depth of capability, with autonomy considered separately.
evidence.limit: A framework for describing progress is not a certification that a current model has passed every threshold.

evidence.title: ARC Prize: ARC-AGI-3
evidence.finding: Interactive environments test how agents explore, discover goals and adapt to unfamiliar tasks.
evidence.limit: This measures a particular form of adaptation. A score alone cannot establish competence across all cognitive or economic work.

records.definition: AI systems that autonomously execute multi-step knowledge work across tools, queues and approval boundaries, owning outcomes end-to-end rather than assisting a human operator.
records.reason: Task completion is measurable, but reliable ownership of a workplace process is a broader claim. The dates remain illustrative, with no new adoption probability assigned.

evidence.title: METR: task-completion time horizons
evidence.finding: METR estimates task difficulty at specified success rates, using human completion time as the reference.
evidence.limit: These are mainly well-specified software tasks. A time horizon is not continuous autonomous runtime or proof that a whole job can be automated.

evidence.title: METR: metrics of agent ability
evidence.finding: The research note compares performance measures that account for time, cost and the human baseline.
evidence.limit: It analyses measurement choices. It does not establish widespread enterprise adoption.

records.definition: General-purpose physical robots (humanoid or otherwise) that are commercially routine, not demo-quality, with fleet-deployable reliability and workable unit economics.
records.reason: The July model cards provide concrete evidence of robotics work and its limits. They do not establish fleet economics or commercial general-purpose reliability. The date windows remain illustrative.

evidence.title: Google DeepMind: Gemini Robotics ER 2
evidence.finding: The model card describes spatial and temporal reasoning, tool orchestration and success detection for physical agents.
evidence.limit: The publisher restricts safety-critical uses. Reasoning capability alone does not demonstrate reliable physical deployment.

evidence.title: Google DeepMind: Robotics On-Device 2
evidence.finding: The card describes local robot action generation and evaluations of manipulation across several robot platforms.
evidence.limit: Access is limited to trusted testers. The card identifies limits on unfamiliar tasks and complex robot control.

records.definition: Coding agents reliably owning the loop from ticket to monitored production deploy across large codebases, leaving humans mostly specifying, reviewing and steering.
records.reason: The evidence supports testing useful delegation, with careful measurement of the whole task. It does not establish an arrival year for autonomous production delivery. The original windows remain illustrative.

evidence.title: METR: revising its productivity experiment
evidence.finding: METR reports that selection effects make its later developer experiment an unreliable estimate of the current productivity effect.
evidence.limit: This is a reason to improve measurement. It establishes neither universal slowdown nor a reliable universal speedup.

evidence.title: METR: task-completion methodology
evidence.finding: The published methodology makes the task set, human reference and success thresholds inspectable.
evidence.limit: Successful benchmark tasks do not include every responsibility involved in maintaining a live software service.

records.definition: AI tutoring and assessment displacing institutional course and credential delivery as the primary structure through which people learn and signal mastery.
records.reason: Better tutoring and replacement of institutional education are different claims. The pragmatic case describes improvement within institutions, so it is a partial transformation rather than fulfilment of the full replacement definition. The dates remain illustrative.

evidence.title: Kestin and colleagues: AI tutoring trial
evidence.finding: A randomised trial in undergraduate physics reported higher immediate learning gains with a specifically designed AI tutor than with the comparison lessons.
evidence.limit: A study of selected lessons does not establish long-term learning across subjects, replacement of teachers or a change in credentials.
